title_en: Shanghai Ocean Shipping Company v. Ningbo Health and Quarantine Institute — dispute over administrative penalty for frontier health quarantine

full_text_en:
Shanghai Ocean Shipping Company v. Ningbo Health Quarantine Office — dispute over administrative penalty for border health quarantine

Plaintiff: Shanghai Ocean Shipping Company.
Legal representative: Li Kelin, Manager.

Defendant: Ningbo Health Quarantine Office.
Legal representative: Hong Changhua, Deputy Director.

Plaintiff Shanghai Ocean Shipping Company, dissatisfied with the administrative penalty decision on border health quarantine made by the defendant Ningbo Health Quarantine Office against its vessel "Fushuncheng", filed an administrative lawsuit with the Haishu District People's Court of Ningbo City, Zhejiang Province.

After accepting the case, the Haishu District People's Court, considering that the case had a significant impact in Ningbo City, reported the case to the Ningbo Intermediate People's Court for trial pursuant to Article 23, Paragraph 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The Ningbo Intermediate People's Court decided to try the case.

Plaintiff Shanghai Ocean Shipping Company alleged: The defendant Ningbo Health Quarantine Office, on the grounds that three food and drinking water handlers on the plaintiff's vessel "Fushuncheng" did not hold health certificates issued by the health quarantine authority, and that during entry and exit quarantine inspections, the health quarantine authority pointed this out and requested that procedures for issuing replacement certificates be completed, but the captain refused to replace the certificates and resisted health supervision, made a decision to impose a fine of RMB 4,900. This decision is both contrary to the facts and without legal basis. The plaintiff requested the court to revoke the defendant's penalty decision.

Defendant Ningbo Health Quarantine Office argued: The three food and drinking water handlers on the plaintiff's vessel "Fushuncheng" did not hold health certificates issued by the health quarantine authority and should have undergone procedures for issuing replacement certificates. However, the captain refused on two occasions, which constituted an illegal act. Pursuant to Articles 109 and 110 of the Implementing Rules of the Frontier Health and Quarantine Law of the People's Republic of China, the decision to impose a fine of RMB 4,900 on the plaintiff's vessel "Fushuncheng" was lawful and should be upheld by the court.

Through public trial, the Ningbo Intermediate People's Court found the following facts:

On June 15, 1991, the plaintiff's vessel "Fushuncheng" arrived from Japan at the Zhenhai loading and unloading area of Ningbo. On the same day, the defendant Ningbo Health Quarantine Office conducted entry quarantine inspection on the vessel at Zhenhai Port Area. During the inspection, it was discovered that the vessel's chef Gu Yongkang, second chef Feng Guoqiang, and steward Liu Bo did not hold health certificates issued by the health quarantine authority. The quarantine office immediately requested the vessel to complete procedures for issuing replacement certificates, but the captain refused, on the grounds that the seafarer health certificates held by the three handlers, issued by the Ministry of Communications, were valid. On June 18 of the same month, when conducting exit quarantine inspection on the "Fushuncheng" at Beilun Port Area, the defendant again discovered that the vessel's chef Gu Yongkang, second chef Feng Guoqiang, and steward Liu Bo still did not hold health certificates issued by the health quarantine authority. For this reason, the defendant again requested the vessel to complete procedures for issuing replacement certificates, but the captain refused again, stating that "it is being handled according to superior notice." Thereafter, the three handlers left the country with the vessel. On June 24 of the same month, the defendant, pursuant to Article 109, Item (3) and Article 110, Paragraph 1 of the Implementing Rules of the Frontier Health and Quarantine Law, decided to impose a fine of RMB 4,900 on the plaintiff Shanghai Ocean Shipping Company's vessel "Fushuncheng". The plaintiff, dissatisfied with the defendant's penalty decision, filed an application for administrative reconsideration with the General Quarantine Office of the People's Republic of China on July 15 of the same year. The General Quarantine Office, pursuant to Article 107, Item (3), Article 109, Item (3), and Article 110 of the Implementing Rules of the Frontier Health and Quarantine Law, issued a reconsideration decision on September 11 upholding the fine of RMB 4,900 imposed by Ningbo Health Quarantine Office on the plaintiff. The plaintiff, still dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision of the General Quarantine Office, filed this administrative lawsuit on October 10 of the same year.

The Ningbo Intermediate People's Court held that: Pursuant to Article 107, Item (3) of the Implementing Rules of the Frontier Health and Quarantine Law, which provides that "food and drinking water handlers on entering or exiting means of transport shall hold health certificates issued by the health quarantine authority," the plaintiff Shanghai Ocean Shipping Company's vessel "Fushuncheng" had three food and drinking water handlers—chef Gu Yongkang, second chef Feng Guoqiang, and steward Liu Bo—who were food and drinking water handlers on an entering and exiting means of transport and should have held health certificates issued by the health quarantine authority. However, Gu Yongkang, Feng Guoqiang, and Liu Bo only held seafarer health certificates issued by the Ministry of Communications after physical examinations by Shanghai Ocean Shipping Hospital, which did not comply with the relevant provisions of the Implementing Rules of the Frontier Health and Quarantine Law. When the defendant conducted entry and exit quarantine inspections, it requested the vessel to complete procedures for issuing health certificates, which was an exercise of its quarantine powers according to law, but was twice refused by the plaintiff's captain. Therefore, the defendant's penalty decision imposing a fine of RMB 4,900 on the plaintiff's vessel "Fushuncheng" was lawful.

Accordingly, on January 11, 1992, the Ningbo Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

The administrative penalty decision of the defendant Ningbo Health Quarantine Office against the plaintiff's vessel "Fushuncheng" is affirmed.

After the first-instance judgment, the plaintiff Shanghai Ocean Shipping Company, dissatisfied, appealed to the Zhejiang High People's Court, arguing that the first-instance judgment distorted the relevant facts and applied the law improperly, and requested the court to quash the first-instance judgment and the administrative penalty decision. The appellee Ningbo Health Quarantine Office argued that the first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correct application of law, and requested the court to affirm the first-instance judgment.

The Zhejiang High People's Court held that the three food and drinking water handlers—chef Gu Yongkang, second chef Feng Guoqiang, and steward Liu Bo—on the appellant Shanghai Ocean Shipping Company's vessel "Fushuncheng" did not hold health certificates issued by the health quarantine authority. When the health quarantine authority pointed this out during entry and exit quarantine inspections and requested that procedures for issuing replacement certificates be completed, the captain refused on two occasions and resisted health supervision. These acts violated the relevant provisions of the Frontier Health and Quarantine Law and its Implementing Rules and should be penalized according to law. The administrative penalty decision made by the appellee Ningbo Health Quarantine Office had a legal basis. The first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact, correct application of law, and lawful litigation procedures; its affirmation of the administrative penalty decision of Ningbo Health Quarantine Office was correct. The appeal grounds of Shanghai Ocean Shipping Company could not be sustained. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 61, Item (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment on May 4, 1992:

The appeal of the appellant Shanghai Ocean Shipping Company is dismissed, and the first-instance judgment is affirmed.
